correctness.rationale: The fitted coefficient is the Rayleigh quotient of H=sym(T^{-1}) after y=Tb, and attainable independently by training/test vectors. The exact residual identity gives all-pairs nonexpansion iff M<=2m; extremal-eigenvector construction proves necessity. H=(I+C_n(t))/2 with standard KMS Toeplitz C; a Poisson-kernel integral gives strict spectral bounds yielding t<=1/3 and long-path constant/alternating vectors show sharp failure above 1/3. Explicit H2 and H3 spectra give 2/3 and sqrt(3sqrt2-4) boundaries, including equality. A fully rational two-site amplifier and a standalone checker with 961 passing assertions verify key identities without treating finite tests as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 ILU study constructs and reuses a GMRES polynomial but does not give the sharp all-pairs scalar transfer threshold. The full Embree et al. study treats polynomial reuse and has an explicit diagonalizability assumption in its eigenvector transfer bound, inapplicable to the defective triangular family. The classical Kac–Murdock–Szegő matrix and symbol bounds are acknowledged as prior mathematical ingredients; their known spectrum alone does not state the independent training/deployment residual criterion. Related published two-step same-right-hand-side GMRES and ideal affine-Jordan polynomial optimizations impose different constraints. Searches did not locate a covering statement; residual priority risks are explicit.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed statement could characterize all-pair contraction of reused minimum-residual steps or use equivalent accretive inverse language.
Classical Toeplitz and Kac–Murdock–Szegő spectral bounds are known; priority is asserted only for their precise fixed-polynomial transfer application and thresholds, not for the spectrum.
Only the abstract of Joubert (1994) could be inspected; its full text may contain a related general fixed-polynomial bound. The result is not claimed to exclude this possibility.
The original motivating work uses higher polynomial degrees in practice; this degree-zero analysis is a safety boundary for the simplest case, not a validated high-degree performance prediction.

value.rationale: A polynomial generated from a single random right-hand side and reused without dot products is precisely the operational motivation of the recent triangular ILU solver study. The theorem answers a natural all-right-hand-side robustness question: transfer safety is uniform only below sharp coupling 1/3, while a fitted GMRES polynomial can improve its training residual yet increase a second residual. The difference from the sharp size-2 and size-3 cutoffs explains why testing tiny triangular systems is misleading. This is a complete structural classification for a minimal family, not an arbitrary isolated parameter computation; degree-zero scope is explicit.
